From the owner
Many homeowners begin a kitchen remodeling project by asking the same question: should they choose cabinet refacing or cabinet refinishing? While both services improve the appearance of existing cabinets, they achieve different results. Cabinet refinishing focuses on restoring the existing cabinet doors and drawer fronts by sanding, repairing, and applying a new paint or stain. Cabinet refacing, on the other hand, replaces the doors, drawer fronts, and visible exterior surfaces while keeping the cabinet boxes in place. Both options cost less than full cabinet replacement and can dramatically transform a kitchen. Understanding how these services differ helps homeowners make the right investment based on the condition of their cabinets and the look they want to achieve. Professional guidance can ensure your kitchen remodeling project delivers the best possible results.

Dark spots on a ceiling are never just a cosmetic problem. This before-and-after from a recent Overland Park project shows what proper repair looks like. The damaged, discolored section was removed and replaced with fresh panels, clean seams, and a finish that blends right in. Water stains and spotting like this often trace back to a leak, and sometimes they mean the surrounding framing needs wood rot repair before new drywall goes up. As a Home Remodeling Contractor, we take the time to find the real cause instead of just covering it up. The nice part is one crew can handle the whole picture. If the moisture came from a failing window, our window repair and Windows Install services fix that too. If siding damage is letting water in, our siding repair team has it covered. That is the benefit of working with a Window Replacement Contractor and Siding Contractor that does full Remodeling work. ✔ Licensed in Kansas and Missouri ✔ Over 50 years of combined experience ✔ We explain the process before any work begins Fall is a good time to deal with interior repairs before the busy holiday season.
